text:
maya: heads up — automated progressive rollout (redwood-rollout v2 -> v3) in eu-west-1 is stuck at 10% for ~35m. Argo shows Helm sync error on inference-service. Can someone take a look? :eyes:

alex: looking now. which job triggered the rollout? the pipeline shows canary-percentage increments but the controller never advances.

maya: gitops pipeline did the rollout via argo-app-reconcile at 11:02 UTC. rollout controller attempted traffic shift to v3 -> 10% but then stopped. no manual pause.

sanjay: paste of the last helm error from Argo next to the rollout log:

maya: ```
Error: UPGRADE FAILED: rendered manifests contain a resource that already exists.
Disable resource creation or set "helm.sh/resource-policy: keep" for that object in v3 chart.
Name: inference-config, Kind: ConfigMap
```

alex: ah. we recently changed the chart to create inference-config as a separate CR in v3, but tf applied a nodepool label rename last week. if the chart expects nodeSelector: gpu=true and new nodes are labeled gpu:accelerator the service can't schedule and Helm might be trying to recreate a config that already exists under a different name.

sanjay: checking cluster: `kubectl get nodes --show-labels -l gpu` shows nothing in eu-west-1. Nodepool autoscaler label was removed by a terraform change (autoscaling/labels refactor) — likely drift.

deploy-bot: [deploy] progressive-rollout/redwood-inference-service:v3 -> paused (reason: helm-sync-error) at 10% traffic.

maya: ok — so two problems: terraform drift removed the gpu label, and helm chart conflicts on the ConfigMap. both block automations. suggested mitigation?

alex: short-term: force Argo to skip the conflicting object by adding `--resource-ignore` is messy. better: patch the release to set `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep` on the ConfigMap so Helm won't try to recreate it. we can do that with `kubectl annotate configmap inference-config helm.sh/resource-policy=keep` then force a sync.

sanjay: agree. also we should pause the rollout controller so it doesn't keep trying increments while we fix infra. `kubectl -n infra patch rollout redwood-inference --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/paused","value":true}]'`

maya: i'm going to pause it now. done. :white_check_mark:

alex: i'll annotate the configmap and force Argo sync. doing: `kubectl annotate cm inference-config -n infra helm.sh/resource-policy=keep` then in argocd UI -> app -> SYNC -> skip dry-run -> sync.

maya: after that, can we reconcile terraform? i can open a small change to re-add the gpu label to nodepool so pods can schedule.

sanjay: yes but hold on the TF change — we should run `terraform plan` against the eu-west workspace first to confirm drift. quick snippet I saw locally: 

maya: ```
# terraform plan excerpt
- resource "google_container_node_pool" "inference_gpu" {
    - node_config {
        - labels = {
            - "gpu" = "true"
        }
    }
  }

# plan shows labels would be added back (drift present)
```

alex: timeline proposal: 1) pause rollout (done), 2) annotate configmap & force argocd sync (in progress), 3) run terraform apply to restore gpu label (maya), 4) unpause rollout after a health check and a manual 20% bump to validate scheduling, 5) watch automated increments.

maya: i'm on step 3 now, raising TF change PR and will kick a plan. cc @sanjay for validation of node taints/affinities.

sanjay: will validate. also recommend adding a pre-rollout gate in the pipeline to check node label predicates and helm-merge conflicts. tiny script: `kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o name || exit 1` — fail the rollout if not present.

alex: +1. also add argocd hook to fail fast on helm manifest conflicts: check for existing resource names before helm upgrade. prevents partial rollouts.

maya: noted. i'll put both checks in the rollout job and TF PR.

deploy-bot: [action] manual intervention recorded by maya at 1769504489: rollout paused; argo sync forced; tf PR opened: link-to-pr.

sanjay: after TF apply, let's not auto-unpause. manual 20% then monitor 30m for scheduling failures, then allow automated increments.

alex: agreed. also cost note — the nodepool label drift caused our gpu nodes to be underutilized last week; ops flagged a cost blip. once this is fixed we should run a 24h cost check on that pool.

maya: adding to follow-up checklist: postmortem for rollout automation + add node-label precondition + argocd helm conflict detect + cost verification.

sanjay: thanks team. i'll stay on call for validation after TF apply.

maya: thanks all. will update thread when TF apply succeeds and rollout resumes. :rocket:
